 Two teams sitting in the bottom half of the Ligue 1 table, separated by a single point, meet at Stade Francis-Le Blé in a match that carries real weight for both sides. Stade Brestois has found some momentum recently, picking up four points across its last two league fixtures — including a 5-1 dismantling of Angers and a 1-1 draw at Lille. OGC Nice, meanwhile, has dropped its last three away matches in the league, scoring just once across those road trips.
 For Brest, Kamory Doumbia leads the attack with four goals on the season, while Ludovic Ajorque has contributed two goals, one assist, and eight shots on target — a constant physical presence. On the Nice side, Elye Wahi has two goals and six shots on target, and Jonathan Clauss has created 10 chances from his position, making him one of the more dangerous wide contributors in the division. If Nice is going to reverse its road struggles, those two will need to be central to the effort.
 The gap between these clubs in the table is narrow, but the gap in recent confidence is wider. That tension makes for a genuinely compelling watch.

 Game Preview
 Brest sits 16th in the Ligue 1 table with 2 points and a goal differential of -3. Nice is one place below in 17th, with 1 point and an identical -3 goal differential. Neither side has found consistent footing through the early weeks of the campaign, and a result here carries direct implications for both clubs’ positions in the lower reaches of the table. Nice’s away record adds another layer — eight road defeats in the 2026 calendar year, the worst mark in the division — making Brest’s home ground a genuinely difficult destination for Olivier Pantaloni’s side.
 What to Watch For
 Kamory Doumbia is the player Brest builds around right now. Four goals through the early portion of the season put him among the more productive forwards in the league, and Joris Chotard’s 12 chances created give the attack a reliable supply line. Ludovic Ajorque adds a second dimension — two goals, one assist, and eight shots on target suggest a striker who stays involved even when the goals aren’t coming. Brest has yet to keep a clean sheet this season, so the attacking intent is genuine on both sides.
 For Nice, the burden falls on Elye Wahi and the creative work of Jonathan Clauss and Gauthier Hein. Clauss has created 10 chances and Hein nine, yet the team’s away output has been almost nonexistent — one goal across three road matches. Sofiane Diop’s two assists show he can connect play, and Mohamed Amoura has contributed a goal, eight chances created, and consistent pressure in the final third. Whether Nice can finally convert that creativity into road points is the central question this match will answer.
